comparison_tool: schemathesis (direct, against the same NDJSON report)

seed_note: The NDJSON was generated with --max-examples 2 against the
publicly-hosted petstore3 demo to keep the fixture small
(~300 KiB). Hypothesis's default seed varies, but the report
captures one stable snapshot — re-running schemathesis against
the live demo will produce a slightly different set due to
petstore3 server state drift, so we pin THIS report instead
of regenerating per bench run (Codex Phase 2-O MUST-FIX #5).

notes: Phase 2-O parser/bench fixture. The committed NDJSON exercises
blocks). The bench measures that secscan's parser surfaces the
expected check names — the same set Schemathesis itself prints
Live bench against a running petstore3 container is intentionally
NOT part of the default bench: swaggerapi/petstore3:1.0.16 is
linux/amd64-only and times out under Rosetta on Apple Silicon
even after 200 seconds (verified during Phase 2-O smoke). The
committed-report approach gives a deterministic parser test
without needing a working petstore3 launcher.
